typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Chardonnay.

name: Sussex
summary: The centre of England's booming traditional-method sparkling wine, on chalk like Champagne's.
climate: Cool maritime, marginal but warming.
soils: Chalk of the South Downs, greensand and clay.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, Bacchus.

name: Kent
summary: 'The Garden of England', with major sparkling producers on North Downs chalk.
climate: Cool maritime, among England's warmest and driest.
soils: Chalk, clay and greensand.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, Bacchus.

name: Sonoma County
summary: Napa's larger, more varied western neighbour, from the foggy Sonoma Coast to warm Dry Creek and Alexander valleys.
climate: Ranges from cool, fog-bound coastal sites to warm inland valleys.
soils: Very diverse: Goldridge sandy loam, volcanic soils, alluvium and clay.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc.
blends: Old-vine Zinfandel field blends; Bordeaux blends.

name: Russian River Valley
summary: Sonoma AVA shaped by Pacific fog funnelled up the Russian River, renowned for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
climate: Cool, with morning fog and warm afternoons.
soils: Goldridge sandy loam and alluvium.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Zinfandel.

name: Paso Robles
summary: Central Coast AVA between San Francisco and Los Angeles, with eleven sub-AVAs and a Rhône Rangers tradition.
climate: Warm days, cool nights from Pacific air through the Templeton Gap.
soils: Calcareous limestone, shale and sandy loam.
typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre.
blends: GSM and Rhône blends; Cabernet blends.

name: Santa Barbara County
summary: Central Coast area whose east–west valleys (Santa Rita Hills, Santa Maria) channel ocean air; setting of the film Sideways.
climate: Cool maritime near the coast, warmer inland (Happy Canyon).
soils: Sand, diatomaceous earth and clay loam.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Syrah, Grenache, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Santa Cruz Mountains
summary: Rugged AVA south of San Francisco, home of Ridge Monte Bello and Mount Eden.
climate: Cool mountain, above the fog line.
soils: Shale, sandstone and limestone, cut by the San Andreas Fault.
typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Zinfandel.

name: Lodi
summary: Central Valley AVA east of San Francisco Bay with California's largest stock of old-vine Zinfandel.
climate: Warm Mediterranean, cooled by Delta breezes.
soils: Sandy granitic loam.
typical_varietals: Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Petite Sirah.

name: Mendocino
summary: Northern California county including the cool Anderson Valley, known for Pinot Noir, sparkling and old-vine field blends.
climate: Cool coastal to warm inland.
soils: Sandstone, shale and alluvium.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Zinfandel, Carignan, Gewürztraminer.

name: Willamette Valley
summary: Oregon's main region south of Portland, celebrated for Burgundian-style Pinot Noir since the 1960s.
climate: Cool, maritime-influenced, with dry summers and wet winters.
soils: Volcanic Jory, marine sediment Willakenzie and windblown loess.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay.

name: Columbia Valley
summary: Huge, dry AVA covering most of Washington State's vineyards, east of the Cascades.
climate: Semi-arid desert with long, sunny summer days; irrigated.
soils: Windblown loess and sand over flood-deposited basalt.
typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Riesling, Chardonnay.

name: Walla Walla Valley
summary: AVA straddling Washington and Oregon, known for Syrah and Cabernet; includes the cobbled Rocks District.
climate: Semi-arid continental.
soils: Loess, and basalt cobbles in The Rocks.
typical_varietals: Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.

name: Finger Lakes
summary: Glacial lakes in upstate New York, America's leading cool-climate Riesling region.
climate: Cool continental; deep lakes moderate temperatures.
soils: Glacial till, shale and limestone.
typical_varietals: Riesling, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir, Grüner Veltliner.
blends: Dry to sweet Riesling; ice wine.

name: Long Island
summary: North Fork and Hamptons vineyards on New York's Long Island.
climate: Moderate maritime.
soils: Sandy, glacial outwash.
typical_varietals: Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Virginia
summary: Historic state (Jefferson's Monticello) with a growing reputation, especially around Charlottesville.
climate: Humid continental with summer heat and rain.
soils: Granite and greenstone in the Blue Ridge foothills.
typical_varietals: Viognier, Cabernet Franc, Petit Manseng, Petit Verdot, Norton.

name: Niagara Peninsula
summary: Ontario's main region between Lakes Ontario and Erie, world-famous for ice wine.
climate: Cool continental; the Niagara Escarpment and the lakes moderate it.
soils: Clay, loam and limestone.
typical_varietals: Riesling, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Vidal, Pinot Noir.

name: Okanagan Valley
summary: British Columbia's long lake valley, running from desert in the south to cooler lakeside sites in the north.
climate: Semi-arid; hot days, cold nights and northern latitude.
soils: Glacial sands, gravel and silt.
typical_varietals: Merlot, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Syrah.

name: Valle de Guadalupe
summary: Baja California valley near Ensenada producing most of Mexico's wine.
climate: Mediterranean, cooled by Pacific breezes.
soils: Decomposed granite and sand.
typical_varietals: Nebbiolo, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Grenache, Chenin Blanc.

name: Uco Valley
summary: High-altitude Mendoza valley (Tupungato, Tunuyán, San Carlos) at the foot of the Andes, the source of Argentina's finest Malbec.
climate: Cool, dry high desert (900–1,600 m) with intense sunlight and big diurnal ranges.
soils: Alluvial stones, sand and limestone deposits (Paraje Altamira, Gualtallary).
typical_varietals: Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Luján de Cuyo
summary: Historic heart of Mendoza just south of the city, Argentina's first designation of origin, with old-vine Malbec.
climate: Dry continental at 800–1,100 m.
soils: Alluvial soils with clay and stones.
typical_varietals: Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Bonarda.

name: Salta
summary: North-western Calchaquí valleys around Cafayate, with some of the world's highest vineyards (above 3,000 m).
climate: High desert with intense sun, extreme day–night swings.
soils: Sandy, stony alluvium.
typical_varietals: Torrontés, Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat.

name: San Juan
summary: Argentina's second-largest wine province, north of Mendoza, warm and known for Syrah.
climate: Hot and very dry, irrigated from the Andes.
soils: Alluvial sands and clays.
typical_varietals: Syrah, Malbec, Bonarda, Torrontés.

name: Patagonia
summary: Southern Argentina's Río Negro and Neuquén valleys, with cooler, windy conditions and old Pinot Noir and Malbec vines.
climate: Cool, dry and windy, with long sunny days.
soils: Alluvial and sandy soils.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Malbec, Merlot, Semillon.

name: Maipo Valley
summary: Region around Santiago, historic heart of Chilean Cabernet, especially in Alto Maipo at the foot of the Andes.
climate: Warm Mediterranean with cool Andean nights.
soils: Alluvial gravels and stony soils.
typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Merlot, Syrah.

name: Colchagua Valley
summary: Rapel valley sub-region known for rich reds, with Apalta's steep hillside vineyards.
climate: Warm Mediterranean, with coastal influence increasing westwards.
soils: Granite, clay and alluvium.
typical_varietals: Carmenère, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Malbec.

name: Casablanca Valley
summary: Cool coastal valley between Santiago and Valparaíso, pioneered for white wine in the 1980s.
climate: Cool, with morning fog from the Humboldt current.
soils: Sandy clay over granite.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir.

name: San Antonio Valley
summary: Coastal valley including Leyda, within kilometres of the Pacific, making zesty whites and Pinot Noir.
climate: Very cool maritime.
soils: Granite and clay.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Syrah.

name: Maule Valley
summary: Chile's largest region, with old dry-farmed Carignan and País vines.
climate: Mediterranean with more rain than further north.
soils: Granite and volcanic soils.
typical_varietals: Carignan, País, Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère.

name: Itata Valley
summary: Southern region with some of the oldest vines in the Americas, revived for natural-leaning País and Cinsault.
climate: Cool and wet, maritime.
soils: Granite.
typical_varietals: País, Cinsault, Moscatel.

name: Limarí Valley
summary: Northern semi-desert valley with chalky soils unusual for Chile, noted for mineral Chardonnay.
climate: Cool, with morning fog (camanchaca); arid.
soils: Limestone and clay.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Canelones
summary: Region north of Montevideo, making most of Uruguay's wine, famous for Tannat.
climate: Humid, Atlantic-influenced maritime.
soils: Clay-limestone.
typical_varietals: Tannat, Merlot, Albariño, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Serra Gaúcha
summary: Hilly area of Rio Grande do Sul settled by Italian immigrants, Brazil's main region and known for sparkling wine.
climate: Humid subtropical with high rainfall.
soils: Basalt-derived clay.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Moscato.

name: Swartland
summary: Wheat country north of Cape Town transformed by a revolution of old-vine Chenin Blanc and Rhône-style blends.
climate: Hot and dry Mediterranean; dry-farmed bush vines.
soils: Shale, granite and iron-rich clay.
typical_varietals: Chenin Blanc, Syrah, Grenache, Cinsault, Mourvèdre.
blends: Rhône-style red and Cape white blends.

name: Constantia
summary: South Africa's oldest wine area, in the Cape Town suburbs, whose sweet Vin de Constance was celebrated in the eighteenth century.
climate: Cool maritime, from two oceans and Table Mountain's slopes.
soils: Decomposed granite.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon, Muscat de Frontignan.
blends: Vin de Constance (sweet Muscat); Sauvignon Blanc–Semillon.

name: Paarl
summary: Large region north-east of Cape Town under a granite dome, with a broad mix of styles.
climate: Warm Mediterranean.
soils: Granite, sandstone and shale.
typical_varietals: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage.

name: Franschhoek
summary: Mountain valley settled by French Huguenots in 1688, now a food and wine tourism hub.
climate: Warm Mediterranean, enclosed by mountains.
soils: Granite and sandstone alluvium.
typical_varietals: Semillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz.

name: Walker Bay
summary: Coastal area around Hermanus, including the Hemel-en-Aarde valley, famous for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
climate: Cool maritime, cooled by the Atlantic.
soils: Bokkeveld shale and decomposed granite.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Elgin
summary: Cool, high apple-growing valley south-east of Cape Town, making elegant whites and Pinot Noir.
climate: Cool, with altitude and ocean influence.
soils: Bokkeveld shale and Table Mountain sandstone.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling.

name: Robertson
summary: Breede River valley inland of the Cape, 'the valley of wine and roses', known for Chardonnay on limestone.
climate: Hot and dry, irrigated; south-east breezes cool afternoons.
soils: Limestone-rich alluvium.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Colombard, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.

name: Martinborough
summary: Small village sub-region at the southern end of the Wairarapa, about an hour from Wellington, whose terrace vineyards made New Zealand's early reputation for Pinot Noir.
climate: Cool and dry, sheltered from westerly rain by the Rimutaka and Tararua ranges, but exposed to strong spring winds that cut yields.
soils: Free-draining alluvial gravels and silt loams on the Martinborough Terrace.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Syrah.
blends: Mostly varietal; concentrated, savoury Pinot Noir.

name: Gisborne
summary: East-coast North Island region, the first to see the sun each day and a prime source of Chardonnay.
climate: Warm, sunny maritime with autumn rains.
soils: Fertile alluvial loams and clay.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer, Albariño.

name: Nelson
summary: Sunny region at the top of the South Island, west of Marlborough, with small artisan producers.
climate: Sunny maritime, slightly wetter than Marlborough.
soils: Clay-gravel in the Moutere Hills; alluvial Waimea plains.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Pinot Gris.

name: North Canterbury
summary: Region north of Christchurch including Waipara Valley, known for Riesling and Pinot Noir.
climate: Cool and dry, sheltered from easterlies by the Teviotdale Hills.
soils: Limestone, gravel and clay.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay.

name: Auckland
summary: Region around New Zealand's largest city, including Waiheke Island and the Croatian-founded wineries of Kumeu.
climate: Warm, humid maritime.
soils: Clay over sandstone; volcanic soils.
typical_varietals: Chardonnay, Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon.

name: Yamanashi
summary: Prefecture at the foot of Mount Fuji, Japan's wine heartland and home of the delicate Koshu grape.
climate: Continental basin with hot, humid summers and typhoons.
soils: Volcanic and alluvial soils.
typical_varietals: Koshu, Muscat Bailey A, Merlot, Chardonnay.

name: Hokkaido
summary: Japan's northern island, a cool-climate region drawing foreign producers for Pinot Noir.
climate: Cool with snowy winters; less humid than the main island.
soils: Volcanic and clay.
typical_varietals: Pinot Noir, Kerner, Zweigelt, Chardonnay.

name: Ningxia
summary: Region on the eastern foothills of the Helan Mountains, China's best-known quality wine area.
climate: Arid continental with hot summers and freezing winters; vines are buried for winter.
soils: Gravelly, sandy alluvium.
typical_varietals: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Gernischt (Carmenère), Marselan.

name: Nashik
summary: Maharashtra plateau north-east of Mumbai, 'India's wine capital', with most of the country's wineries.
climate: Tropical; altitude and pruning for winter harvest make viticulture possible.
soils: Basalt-derived red and black soils.
typical_varietals: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon.
